 Why in news? 
 World Children's Day is observed on 20 November every year to promote awareness about children's rights, welfare and protection. 
 Key Facts 
 Particular 
 Details 
 Observance 
 World Children's Day 
 Date 
 20 November 
 Established by

 Established in 
 1954

 2026 Theme 
 My Day. My Rights. My Future. 
 National Children's Day (India) 
 14 November 
 Historical Background 
 Origin of World Children's Day 
 In 1954, the United Nations General Assembly recommended the establishment of Universal Children's Day. 
 The objective was to promote worldwide fraternity, understanding among children and activities supporting children's welfare. 
 The observance was intended to encourage countries to improve the living conditions and opportunities available to children. 
 Declaration of the Rights of the Child, 1959 
 On 20 November 1959, the UN General Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of the Child. 
 It recognised the need for special protection and care for children. 
 The declaration contained 10 principles focusing on education, healthcare, equality, protection and development. 
 It provided an important foundation for the development of international child rights standards. 
 Convention on the Rights of the Child, 1989 
 On 20 November 1989, the UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC). 
 It established a comprehensive framework for protecting children's civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights. 
 The Convention entered into force on 2 September 1990. 
 It recognised children as independent rights-holders rather than merely recipients of welfare and protection. 
 India's Association with UNCRC 
 India ratified the Convention on the Rights of the Child on 11 December 1992. 
 India committed itself to protecting children's rights through appropriate legislative, administrative and policy measures. 
 The Convention has influenced India's child protection laws, educational policies and welfare programmes. 
 Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) 
 The UNCRC is an international human rights treaty that establishes the rights of every child. 
 It defines a child as every human being below 18 years of age, unless majority is attained earlier under applicable law. 
 It consists of 54 Articles covering different aspects of children's lives. 
 It is the most widely ratified international human rights treaty. 
 Four Fundamental Principles of UNCRC 
 Principle 
 Significance 
 Non-discrimination (Article 2) 
 All children must enjoy equal rights without discrimination. 
 Best Interests of the Child (Article 3) 
 Children's welfare must be a primary consideration in decisions affecting them. 
 Right to Life, Survival and Development (Article 6) 
 Every child has the right to life, survival and healthy development. 
 Respect for Children's Views (Article 12) 
 Children have the right to express their opinions and be heard. 
 Four Major Categories of Children's Rights 
 Survival Rights : Right to life, nutrition, healthcare and adequate living conditions. 
 Development Rights: Right to education, recreation, information and cultural activities. 
 Protection Rights: Protection from abuse, exploitation, trafficking, violence and neglect. 
 Participation Rights : Right to freedom of expression and participation in decisions affecting their lives. 
 Major Challenges Affecting Children 
 Child Poverty: Economic inequality restricts access to education, healthcare, nutrition and safe living conditions. 
 Child Labour: Children engaged in hazardous work are deprived of education and healthy development. 
 Malnutrition: Undernutrition, stunting, wasting and micronutrient deficiencies affect children's physical and cognitive development. 
 Child Marriage: Early marriage affects education, health and personal development, particularly among girls. 
 Child Abuse and Exploitation: Physical abuse, sexual violence, trafficking and neglect threaten children's safety. 
 Digital Risks : Cyberbullying, online grooming and exploitation create new challenges for child protection. 
 Climate Change: Floods, droughts, heatwaves and air pollution adversely affect children's health, education and living conditions. 
 Child Rights in India: Constitutional Provisions 
 Article 
 Constitutional provision 
 Article 14 
 Equality before law and equal protection of laws. 
 Article 15(3) 
 Special provisions for women and children. 
 Article 21 
 Protection of life and personal liberty. 
 Article 21A 
 Free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years. 
 Article 23 
 Prohibition of trafficking and forced labour. 
 Article 24 
 Prohibition of employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines and hazardous employment. 
 Article 39(e) 
 Protection of children's tender age and health against abuse. 
 Article 39(f) 
 Opportunities for healthy development and protection against exploitation and abandonment. 
 Article 45 
 Early childhood care and education for children below six years. 
 Article 47 
 Improvement of nutrition levels and public health. 
 Important Laws for Child Protection in India 
 Right to Education Act, 2009: Provides free and compulsory elementary education to children aged 6–14 years. 
 POCSO Act, 2012: Protects children from sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography-related offences. 
 Juvenile Justice Act, 2015: Provides care, protection, rehabilitation and social reintegration of children. 
 Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006: Prohibits child marriage and provides legal remedies and penalties. 
 Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986: Prohibits employment of children below 14 years, subject to specified exceptions, and prohibits adolescents from hazardous occupations and processes. 
 Major Government Initiatives for Child Welfare 
 Scheme / Initiative 
 Objective 
 Mission Vatsalya 
 Child protection, care, rehabilitation and welfare of vulnerable children. 
 POSHAN Abhiyaan 
 Improve nutritional outcomes among children and women. 
 Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 
 Strengthen nutrition and early childhood care services. 
 PM POSHAN 
 Nutritional support through meals for eligible schoolchildren. 
 Samagra Shiksha 
 Improve access, equity and quality of school education. 
 Beti Bachao Beti Padhao 
 Promote survival, protection and education of the girl child. 
 Palna Scheme 
 Provide crèche facilities and childcare services. 
 PM CARES for Children 
 Support eligible children who lost parents or guardians due to COVID-19. 
 International Organisations Working for Child Welfare 
 UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund): Works towards children's health, education, nutrition, protection and overall development. 
 UNESCO: Promotes inclusive and equitable quality education. 
 WHO: Works on child healthcare, immunisation and disease prevention. 
 ILO: Works towards eliminating child labour and promoting decent work. 
 UN Committee on the Rights of the Child: Monitors the implementation of UNCRC by its State Parties. 
 Prelims MCQ 
 Q. Consider the following statements regarding the Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC): 
 It was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 1989. 
 It consists of 54 Articles. 
 India ratified the Convention in 1992. 
 It applies only to children below 14 years of age. 
 Which of the statements given above are correct? 
 (a) 1 and 2 only 
 (b) 1, 2 and 3 only 
 (c) 2, 3 and 4 only 
 (d) 1, 2, 3 and 4 
 Mains Practice Question 
 Q. Discuss the significance of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in strengthening child protection mechanisms in India. 
 FAQs 
 1. When is World Children's Day celebrated? 
 20 November. 
 2. When was World Children's Day established? 
 1954 by the United Nations General Assembly. 
 3. What is the theme of World Children's Day 2026? 
 My Day. My Rights. My Future. 
 4. When was the UNCRC adopted? 
 20 November 1989. 
 5. When did India ratify the UNCRC? 
 11 December 1992.
